Control any real iPhone using multimodal vision models and a $7 ESP32 microcontroller, completely bypassing Macs, Xcode, jailbreaks, and developer account restrictions! 🤯

Building AI agents that interact with mobile devices usually means wrestling with expensive desktop emulators, restricted software test runners, or messy code-signing certificates. 

The esp32-iphone-agent project changes the game by giving AI vision models physical "eyes" and "hands" to control real iOS devices completely autonomously, without needing any helper apps installed on the phone.

Here is how it works:
👁️ Eyes: Real-time screen mirroring captured via UxPlay and GStreamer feeds the AI visual feedback so it can verify tap locations and self-correct pointer drift.
🖐️ Hands: A Wi-Fi-connected ESP32-S3 microcontroller acts as a standard USB HID mouse and keyboard plugged right into the iPhone port, mapping inputs directly to iOS AssistiveTouch.
🧠 Brain: A decoupled planner and actor architecture supporting any OpenAI-compatible vision model, running on cloud APIs or local hardware.
💻 Control Center: A full web UI featuring live interaction controls, a step wall showing screenshot history with action overlays, and an emergency stop mechanism.

Whether you want to build automated end-to-end mobile app testing across a fleet of physical devices or create a personal assistant for repetitive cross-app workflows, this is the ultimate hardware-in-the-loop blueprint.

Check out the repo and start building your own physical-world GUI agents today:
https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent

🔥 Play Diablo II: Resurrected natively on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS at a rock-solid 60 fps—with zero CPU emulation! 

For years, bringing complex desktop and console AAA games to mobile hardware meant dealing with heavy CPU emulation or relying on laggy cloud streaming. 

`jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile` changes the game. It takes the original aarch64 game binary and executes it directly on Apple Silicon. By supplying a custom host layer for system calls, audio, file I/O, and Apple Metal graphics, it achieves native performance while sipping battery at roughly 3.8 Watts.

Here is what makes this project a masterclass in systems and graphics engineering:

⚡ Native Binary Execution: Direct execution of aarch64 binaries with zero emulation overhead, paired with offline shader translation straight to Apple Metal.
🎮 Touch-First Redesign: Completely re-imagined controls mapping classic desktop inputs to intuitive mobile gestures, edge-to-edge layouts, and contextual dual-skill buttons.
🔋 Extreme Thermal Efficiency: Tuned for mobile constraints to maintain a steady 60 fps without cooking your device.

Why should you check it out? 
Whether you are a graphics engineer working with Apple Metal, a game engine developer, or a systems programmer, this repository serves as an incredible architectural reference for reverse-engineering console-to-mobile ports, writing native API translation layers, and building offline shader compilation pipelines.

Dive into the source code and start exploring today:
https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile

🤖 Transform DeepSeek Harness into a multi-agent orchestration layer featuring autonomous bot-to-bot messaging, group chats, and persistent agent memory!

Are you tired of raw model endpoints that lack continuity, collaboration, and real teamwork? 

The DeepSeek-Bot repository extends the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem by introducing long-lived multi-agent frameworks. It turns standalone models into persistent, collaborative bots capable of handling group chats, delegating sub-tasks via mention relays, managing individual memory stores, and coordinating complex workflows through a chief orchestrator bot.

🔥 Key Features:
• Hierarchical multi-agent group chats with admin routing, direct @mentions, and bot-to-bot task handoffs.
• Persistent agent memory that stores user preferences and contextual history locally across sessions.
• Shared capabilities library supporting Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, modular skills, and custom tool packs.
• Local-first data architecture storing all session data, state, and memory locally inside your own environment.

💡 Perfect for orchestrating specialized teams of AI agents (like Chief, Writer, and Coder) to solve complex software tasks, or for building privacy-focused automation pipelines where your code never leaves your hardware.

Explore the code, study advanced multi-agent orchestration patterns, and build your own local-first agent ecosystem today.

👉 Check it out on GitHub: https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot

Tired of workspace pollution, credential leaks, and the headache of managing multiple Claude identities across projects? 

Meet CCBaga: a lightning-fast native Rust and Tauri desktop toolkit built specifically for developers, AI engineers, and remote contractors who need totally isolated environments, verifiable browser fingerprints, and seamless multi-account management. 🚀

Whether you are switching between distinct localized Claude CLI setups or running automated AI tasks that require strict regional configurations, CCBaga eliminates cross-contamination of cache and auth data without the heavy overhead of virtualization.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your workflow:

🔒 Encrypted Identity Management: Securely archive and restore Claude Code and Claude Desktop states into compressed .baga containers with atomic rollbacks.
🌐 Automated Browser Fingerprint Rotation: Sync regional languages, timezones, and hardware attributes instantly with a companion Chromium instance.
🔍 Real-Time Telemetry Checks: Validate your local machine readings against actual network exits before executing critical tasks.
🤖 AI-Guided Network Setup: Rapidly deploy across coding agents using standard agent skills specifications.

Ready to streamline your multi-account workflow and lock down your dev environments? 

Check out the repo and get started today:
https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga
